subject: North Asia micro-region dedicated capacity: proposal & sizing ask
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: North Asia micro-region dedicated capacity: proposal & sizing ask

Hi team,

LatticeX has come back with a firm request to run their production traffic out of a Tokyo-preferrred micro-region with Singapore as a failover. They want dedicated capacity (no shared tenants) with strict p95 latency targets (~120ms) for their chat endpoints and an SLO for 99.9% uptime. They are planning a staged ramp over 8 weeks starting mid-May.

Quick summary of the ask and our initial sizing proposal:

- Expected steady-state: 800 qps at average request size 1.5k input + 200 tokens output (~300k tokens/min)
- Peak (qoq ramp windows): 2,400 qps sustained for 30-90 minutes during marketing events
- Model profile: finetuned Llama2-like 70B; we expect to serve quantized FP8/INT8 variants with KV cache, typical latency budget 80-120ms

Preliminary capacity translation (rough):
- Steady-state: 6 x H100-80GB equiv (or 24 x A100-40GB equiv)
- Peak buffer: additional 6 x H100 (bring total to 12) for 12-18 hour windows
- Disk and network: local NVMe for prefix/KV cache; 100Gbps networking per node

Operational asks:
- Reserve a Tokyo micro-pool with at least 6 H100-equivalent GPUs committed starting 2027-05-15, with scaling headroom to 12 within 48h
- Singapore site configured as async fallback with 4 H100-equivalent for routing during region failures
- SLA: 99.9% uptime + optional burst credits for the first 3 months

Attachments: I've attached a sizing workbook and LatticeX's Q1 traffic export for your math.

Next steps: Rishi — can you validate the H100/A100 conversion and confirm if 6-card baseline is feasible operationally? Hannah — can you flag any constraints with APAC sourcing (partner procurement, lead times)?

Thanks,
Jonas

-- 
Jonas Weber
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Apr 7, 2027 at 9:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> LatticeX has come back with a firm request...

Got it — this is detailed, thanks. Quick notes/questions:

- The H100-equivalents are fine as a planning unit; operationally we'll translate to node types (4xH100 per node or 8xA100) depending on vendor availability. Lead time for an H100 node in Tokyo is currently ~6-8 weeks unless we reserve via partner
- For the 12-GPU peak, do we need 12 dedicated GPU cards or can we rely on burst-shared capacity from Dedicated Burst (tiered) for the short windows? If strictly dedicated by contract, we should lock 12
- Cost implication for customer: baseline + burst credits model or commit monthly? Jonas, what's their willingness to commit (12-month vs 3-month)?

Operational ask to Hannah: please check supplier lead times (SoftBank cloud partner and our OEM resellers) and confirm whether we can secure initial 6 GPUs by 2027-05-15. If not, propose a fallback (mix of Singapore warm standby + fast-routing policy).

I'll run the workbook assumptions tomorrow and send a spreadsheet with node-level mapping.

- Rishi
From: Hana Kim <hana@latticex.ai>

Cc: procure@orionai.com
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2027 23:05:00 +0900

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick proposal. Confirming LatticeX is comfortable with a 6->12 ramp and prefers a monthly commit rather than annual for the pilot. Two clarifications:

1) Can you guarantee p95 under 150ms for the Tokyo pool specifically? We can accept 99.9% if the latency target is met.
2) End-of-quarter (May 28-31) is our big push — we anticipate a 3x spike over the stated peak. Can you include a runbook for scaling during that window and an estimate for extra cost (overtime burst) if we need 24 H100-equivalent temporarily?

We are starting procurement approvals this week; having a firm start date is helpful.

Best,
Hana
Head of Platform, LatticeX
